encounters_notes_n: study period in full text

study: Duggan et al, JAMA Network Open 2025
encounters_notes_n: outpatient appointments Apr to Jun 2024 (count in full text)
outcomes_as_reported: Time in notes per appointment fell 20.4%, from 10.3 to 8.2 min (p<.001); same-day closure rose 9.3%, from 66.2% to 72.4% (p<.001); after-hours work fell 30.0%, from 50.6 to 35.4 min per workday (p=.02)
error_audit: none reported

study: Biro et al, JMIR 2025 (instrument validation, research letter)
design: error audit (recordings of real encounters read as scripts)
setting: simulated readings of 11 real encounter scripts
product: 2 commercial ambient digital scribe products (A and B)
encounters_notes_n: 44 draft notes (11 scripts x 2 products x 2 readings as printed)
outcomes_as_reported: Instrument validation: error frequency and pattern per product
error_audit: 127 errors in total (mean 2.9, SD 2.7 per draft note); errors in 31 of 44 notes (70%); product A 66 errors (mean 3.0, SD 2.7), product B 61 (mean 2.8, SD 2.7); omissions the most frequent type; error type distribution differed by product (Fisher exact p=.002)
funding_vendor: National Center for Human Factors in Healthcare, MedStar (authors' affiliation); vendor role not stated

study: Balloch et al, Future Healthcare Journal 2024
design: standardised audit (simulated actor consultations, crossover sessions)
product: TORTUS AI ambient tool vs standard EHR practice
encounters_notes_n: 42 consultations
outcomes_as_reported: Consultation and documentation within 20-min sessions; SAIL quality scores for AI vs standard practice (in full text); 100% of clinicians reported full patient attention with the AI tool vs 66% with EHR alone
error_audit: Possible minor hallucination rate about 0.5% and major about 0.21% of about 50 clinical entities per note (as printed); a development retest reported major hallucinations 0% and minor 0.21%
funding_vendor: Authors include TORTUS AI staff (vendor study)

study: Nawaz et al, medRxiv preprint 2025
product: ambient AI scribe (Lyrebird-type tool as reported)
encounters_notes_n: paired simulated stations (8 paired observations)
outcomes_as_reported: NASA-TLX total 25.0 with AI scribe vs 461.3 traditional (mean difference 436.25, 95% CI 389.93 to 482.57, p<0.001) on the paper's summed scale; screen time 5.31 vs 7.46 min (difference -2.15, p=0.27); SAIL documentation quality also measured (scores in full text); satisfaction 100% vs 50%
error_audit: SAIL quality only; no error counts
funding_vendor: preprint; funding as stated in the preprint

study: Pollak et al 2026 (Duke SCRIBE evaluation)
product: AI scribe (GPT-generated notes in the evaluation)
encounters_notes_n: 232 recorded encounters (8 per clinician)
outcomes_as_reported: Burnout by Copenhagen Burnout Inventory; communication coding of recordings (reflective statements, open questions, empathic responses); patient satisfaction (estimates in full text)
error_audit: transcript word error rate 1.4% and speaker alignment precision 92.3% on 20 manually reviewed transcripts (as printed)

study: De John et al, Research Square preprint 2026
product: ambient AI scribe vs handwritten notes
encounters_notes_n: 49 encounters analysed (53 recorded)
outcomes_as_reported: SOAP rubric overall score: AI mean 4.9 vs handwritten 2.9; AI notes better in 48 of 49 encounters; posterior probability of superior AI quality 97.1% (95% CrI 91.0 to 99.8)
error_audit: Omissions: AI 15 events vs handwritten 131; hallucinations AI 21 vs handwritten 23, with handwritten hallucinations more severe (grade 3 median RR 16.2, 95% CrI 3.76 to 184.0)
funding_vendor: vendor-linked author (GraiLabs) in the byline; preprint
